full_text_en:
Beijing Boiler Factory v. Pan Daiming — Dispute over Patent Ownership (Appeal)

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Pan Daiming, male, 60 years old, retired worker of Beijing Boiler Factory.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Qingtai, lawyer of China Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Hong, cadre of China Association for the Application and Exchange of Foreign Technology.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Beijing Boiler Factory.

Legal representative: Zhang Zhiwei, factory director.

Agent ad litem: Liang Xinsheng, cadre of Beijing Boiler Factory.

Agent ad litem: Yang Guang, lawyer of the Legal Advisory Office of the Second Artillery Corps of the Chinese People's Liberation Army.

The civil judgment (1990) Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 174 was rendered by the Beijing Intermediate People's Court on December 3, 1993, concerning the dispute over patent ownership filed by the original plaintiff Beijing Boiler Factory against the defendant Pan Daiming. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Pan Daiming refused to accept it and filed an appeal with the Beijing High People's Court.

The facts found by the court of first instance are as follows: The plaintiff, Beijing Boiler Factory, is a wholly state-owned enterprise. The defendant, Pan Daiming, was a truck driver at the enterprise. In April 1980, Beijing Boiler Factory formally initiated a research project focusing on energy conservation through furnace modification and operational methods. The main contents were: (1) furnace structure modification — "Flat-body Heat Storage Steel Plate Heating Furnace"; (2) adoption of a sequential batch operation method — "Hot Stamping Head Sequential Batch Operation Method." Pan Daiming, as a non-specialized technical staff member of Beijing Boiler Factory, together with four colleagues from the factory's Technology Department, Labor Department, Chief Engineer's Office, and Hydraulic Press Team, under the factory's organization and arrangement, used both working and spare time to jointly develop and formulate a relatively complete test plan and technical scheme. Approved by Beijing Boiler Factory, it was decided to conduct tests on the 800-ton hydraulic press heating furnace on April 20, 1980, with the Hydraulic Press Team of the Drum Workshop as the main body and Pan Daiming and others participating as instructors. Later, tests were also conducted on the 2,500-ton hydraulic press heating furnace. On October 15 and 61 [sic], 1984, the Energy Bureau of the State Economic Commission entrusted the Beijing Municipal Government Energy Conservation Office to organize dozens of experts and technicians to hold an energy-saving technical appraisal meeting at Beijing Boiler Factory. Technical appraisals were conducted on the technologies developed and researched by the factory — "Flat-body Heat Storage Steel Plate Heating Furnace" and "Hot Stamping Head Sequential Batch Operation Method" — and appraisal certificates were issued. The appraisal conclusion was: the energy-saving effect was good, the technical and economic benefits were significant, and it had promotional value. On April 1, 1985, Pan Daiming combined the two aforementioned technologies, renamed them "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof," and filed an invention patent application with the China Patent Office. On March 3, 1988, the application was granted an invention patent, Patent No. 85102032. When Pan Daiming applied for the invention patent, Beijing Boiler Factory, without the approval of the superior competent authority, issued a certificate of non-service invention to the China Patent Office. Pan Daiming's claim that as early as the 1970s he had used his spare time to develop and form the complete technical scheme of Patent No. 85102032 was not substantiated by evidence.

Based on the above facts, the court of first instance held that the patent technology in dispute between Beijing Boiler Factory and Pan Daiming, Patent No. 85102032, was indeed a technical innovation project formally initiated by Beijing Boiler Factory in early 1980, which involved organizing multiple personnel within the factory to participate in research during working hours and utilizing important factory equipment and funds for experimentation and implementation. In accordance with Article 6 of the Technology Contract Law of the PRC and Article 4 of the Implementing Regulations of the Technology Contract Law of the PRC, this patent technology fully possessed the statutory elements of a service technological achievement and should be confirmed as such. Pan Daiming's insistence that the patent technology had been developed by him alone using his spare time and personal funds into a complete technical scheme in the 1970s was not supported by evidence and was therefore not accepted. As a wholly state-owned enterprise, Beijing Boiler Factory, when in possession of the above service technological achievement, issued a certificate of non-service invention to Pan Daiming without the approval of the superior competent authority, thereby transferring the patent application right of this service technological achievement to Pan Daiming, enabling him to obtain the patent application right for this technology. This violated the provisions of Article 10 of the Patent Law of the PRC, which requires that the transfer of the patent application right or patent right by a wholly state-owned unit must be approved by the superior competent authority. Therefore, the act of issuing the certificate was an invalid civil act, and Beijing Boiler Factory should bear primary responsibility. The invention patent right of Patent No. 85102032 in dispute between Beijing Boiler Factory and Pan Daiming should, based on its nature as a service technology, be re-confirmed as held by Beijing Boiler Factory, with Pan Daiming listed as an inventor of the patented technology. The funds, time, and effort expended by Pan Daiming in applying for this patent should be appropriately compensated by Beijing Boiler Factory. Beijing Boiler Factory could not claim the income obtained by Pan Daiming from the patent technology after he acquired the patent right. Accordingly, the court ruled: (1) The invention patent right of Patent No. 85102032, "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof," originally owned by Pan Daiming, was changed to be held by Beijing Boiler Factory; (2) Beijing Boiler Factory was to compensate Pan Daiming for economic losses in the amount of RMB 20,000.

The appellant, Pan Daiming, refused to accept the judgment of first instance and filed an appeal on the following grounds: This case had exceeded the statutory two-year statute of limitations. The grant date of Patent No. 85102032 was March 3, 1988, while the appellee, Beijing Boiler Factory, filed the lawsuit on March 8, 1990. The appellee's claim was to request the court to determine that Patent No. 85102032 was a service technological achievement, but the judgment of first instance changed it to a dispute over patent ownership, exceeding the scope of the parties' request. The court of first instance had made errors in fact-finding. The conception of Patent No. 85102032 was completed by the appellant. There was no patent application right transfer relationship between the appellant and Beijing Boiler Factory. Accordingly, the appellant requested the court of second instance to set aside the original judgment. Beijing Boiler Factory submitted to the judgment of first instance.

The Beijing High People's Court found upon further trial that on April 1, 1985, the appellant, Pan Daiming, filed an invention patent application with the China Patent Office for "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof." On March 3, 1988, the application was granted an invention patent, Patent No. 85102032. On February 10, 1989, Pan Daiming filed a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court against Beijing Babcock & Wilcox Co., Ltd. (a joint venture between the appellee Beijing Boiler Factory and the U.S. Babcock & Wilcox Company) for patent infringement. The Beijing Intermediate People's Court added Beijing Boiler Factory as a co-defendant. During the trial of the patent infringement case, on March 2, 1990, Beijing Boiler Factory submitted a "new claim" to the Beijing Intermediate People's Court, requesting the court to "confirm that Pan Daiming's patented technology was a service invention completed during his work at the factory." However, the factory did not formally file a lawsuit with the Beijing Intermediate People's Court until March 8, 1990, requesting confirmation that Pan Daiming's non-service invention patent No. 85102032 was a service invention achievement. The court of first instance, considering that the patent infringement lawsuit must be based on the outcome of the patent ownership case, suspended the lawsuit filed by Pan Daiming against the joint venture of the U.S. Babcock & Wilcox Company in accordance with Article 136, paragraph 1, item (5) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and separately filed a case with Beijing Boiler Factory as the plaintiff and Pan Daiming as the defendant for patent ownership dispute. During the trial, on October 20, 1992, Beijing Boiler Factory submitted a "Supplemental Civil Claim Petition" to the court of first instance, requesting the court to "judge that Pan Daiming's non-service invention patent No. 85102032 is a service invention patent of Beijing Boiler Factory." The reason given was: "Previously, our factory in the 'Complaint' only requested the court to confirm that Pan Daiming's Patent No. 85102032 was a service invention achievement, without expressing a claim for the patent right. Now it appears that this is not sufficiently complete. Therefore, we hereby add the above claim."

The Beijing High People's Court held as follows:

Regarding the factual findings challenged by the appellant Pan Daiming in his appeal: The court of first instance found in its judgment that the appellee Beijing Boiler Factory formally initiated a research project in the factory in April 1980 on furnace modification and operational methods. However, in the case file of the first instance, there was no evidence from Beijing Boiler Factory concerning the initiation of research on this technology. During the court hearing, Beijing Boiler Factory still stated that it could not provide such evidence to the court. Although Beijing Boiler Factory provided a large amount of materials to the court of first instance, they were unrelated to the project initiation and development of the "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof"; rather, they were records of the implementation of this technical concept in the factory and materials related to the appraisal of the technical scheme. Pan Daiming provided examples from the late 1970s where he applied a technical concept he called the "Ascending-Select-Descending Method" to road paving, buried cable laying, truck transportation, cafeteria management, etc., resulting in increased work efficiency, to demonstrate that the concept of the technical scheme had already been conceived in the 1970s and had been basically completed before 1980. Upon investigation, at the end of 1979, Pan Daiming, under the title "Party Member's Suggestion, Mass Feedback," proposed that Beijing Boiler Factory implement a scheme he called "Labor Efficiency Ascending-Descending Retention" within subordinate workshops, departments, and units, which was essentially a trial of his "Ascending-Select-Descending Method" technical scheme. Upon his suggestion, the factory decided in April 1980 to establish an energy-saving team within the Comprehensive Utilization Department, with Pan Daiming participating, and with Pan Daiming as the lead, began trial application of Pan Daiming's technical scheme on the 800-ton hydraulic press. After the trial succeeded, it was also applied on the 2,500-ton hydraulic press, resulting in a significant increase in work efficiency and economic benefits. In a subsequent summary of the activity, Beijing Boiler Factory not only fully affirmed the energy-saving and efficiency-enhancing effects of the technical scheme but also fully recognized Pan Daiming's role. The *Beiguo Workers' Newspaper* also published extensive reports and gave high praise to Pan Daiming's invention and creation. On April 1, 1985, after Pan Daiming applied for an invention patent for the technology, on June 3, 1985, Beijing Boiler Factory issued a "certificate of non-service invention" to facilitate Pan Daiming's application for a reduction in patent application fees. The time of conception and completion of a technical scheme is not the same as the time it is perfected and made feasible through actual use. The implementation of Pan Daiming's "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof" at Beijing Boiler Factory was for the purpose of making the technology practically applicable and achieving the expected effects at the conception stage of the technology. Therefore, the completion of the technical concept and the specific implementation of the technology are two different issues. This is the key to correctly determining the ownership of the patent right. Pan Daiming's "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof" had already been conceived before 1980, though it was not yet mature at that time and had not undergone feasibility experiments; moreover, the name of the technology was then called by Pan Daiming himself as the "Ascending-Select-Descending Method." After implementation at Beijing Boiler Factory in April 1980 and achieving success, Pan Daiming further summarized the technical scheme transplanted onto the heating furnace, later naming it "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof" and applied for an invention patent.

Article 6 of the Patent Law provides that for a service invention-creation made by a person in the execution of the tasks of the entity to which he belongs or mainly by using the material conditions of the entity, the right to apply for a patent belongs to the entity. After the application is approved, if the application was filed by a wholly state-owned unit, the patent right shall be held by that unit. The appellant, Pan Daiming, was an ordinary truck driver at Beijing Boiler Factory. His initial technical concept, the "Ascending-Select-Descending Method," was not executed as a research task of the appellee Beijing Boiler Factory, nor was it his job duty. Throughout the completion of the concept, he did not use the factory's material conditions or technical materials not publicly available. The trials conducted by Beijing Boiler Factory in April 1980 on the 800-ton and 2,500-ton hydraulic presses were essentially the practical application of Pan Daiming's "Ascending-Select-Descending Method" at the factory, not the use of the factory's equipment conditions to complete Pan Daiming's technical concept. Therefore, in the absence of evidence that Beijing Boiler Factory formally initiated the development of the "Kang-type Heating Furnace and Method of Use thereof," the court of first instance's determination that the invention was a service invention-creation and its judgment that the patent right for the invention should be held by Beijing Boiler Factory lacked legal and factual basis. Furthermore, the court of first instance's characterization of Beijing Boiler Factory's issuance of the certificate of non-service invention to Pan Daiming on June 3, 1985, as a transfer of the patent application right was inconsistent with the facts. Article 10, paragraph 4 of the Patent Law stipulates that for the transfer of the patent application right or the patent right, the parties must conclude a written contract, which shall take effect after it is registered and announced by the Patent Office. However, no patent application right transfer contract was ever concluded between Beijing Boiler Factory and Pan Daiming. The certificate of non-service invention issued by the factory was merely a document for Pan Daiming to apply for a reduction of patent application fees; it did not have the nature of transferring civil rights, nor did it contain any content of rights transfer, nor was there any expression of intent by the parties to transfer or accept the patent application right. Therefore, the certificate issued by Beijing Boiler Factory could not be deemed an act of transferring the patent application right.

Regarding the statute of limitations issue raised by the appellant Pan Daiming in his appeal: Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides that the limitation of action for applying to a people's court for protection of civil rights is two years, unless otherwise provided by law. Article 137 provides that the limitation of action shall begin from the time when the person knows or should know that his rights have been infringed. This case is a dispute over patent ownership, which does not fall within the circumstances otherwise provided by law. Therefore, for Beijing Boiler Factory's claim seeking confirmation that Patent No. 85102032 is a service invention patent and that the patent right is held by the factory, the statute of limitations should be two years, calculated from the date of patent grant on March 3, 1988. On March 2, 1990, Beijing Boiler Factory raised a "new claim" in the patent infringement lawsuit, but the claim did not seek to have Pan Daiming's non-service invention patent confirmed as a service invention patent. On March 8, 1990, when Beijing Boiler Factory formally filed a claim with the court requesting confirmation that Pan Daiming's non-service invention patent was a service invention achievement of the factory, the content of the claim was still not precise, and moreover, it had already exceeded the statutory limitation period. On October 20, 1992, in the supplemental civil claim petition submitted by Beijing Boiler Factory to the court, it finally explicitly requested that Pan Daiming's non-service invention patent be adjudged as a service invention patent of Beijing Boiler Factory. However, by that time, the statutory limitation period had already expired by as much as seven months. Therefore, this court does not support the claim filed by Beijing Boiler Factory. Based on the above findings, the judgment of the court of first instance had unclear factual findings, insufficient evidence, erroneous application of law, and exceeded the statute of limitations. In accordance with Articles 153, items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, on March 23, 1995, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (1990) Zhong Jing Chu Zi No. 174 of the Beijing Intermediate People's Court is set aside.

2. The claim of the appellee, Beijing Boiler Factory, is dismissed.

Litigation fees for the first instance and the second instance, each RMB 1,210, shall be borne by Beijing Boiler Factory.
